p4_b2.ocr: IR active in-plane porphyrin ring vibrations. There are no b1u (a2u) out-of-plane vibrations in the H2P (ZnP) molecules with frequencies larger than 854 cm-1 (Tables 3 and 4). The same was found in calculations of the porphyrin ring out-of-plane vibrations in the tetraphenyl derivatives. Thus, the remainder of the porphyrin IR spectrum is caused by in-plane vibrations, for which assignment and numeration of Li and Zhierski [20] are available. (Here, this numeration is denoted by a prime symbol ’i in order to avoid confusion with our complete numeration including also out-of-plane vibrations.) Analyses of the in-plane vibrations were also reported in a large number of experimental studies [32- 34,37,54,57]. We introduce the discussion of the vibrational structure with the ZnP analysis since it is more convenient to consider first the degenerate eu vibrations, and then to discuss the corresponding vibrations of lower symmetry that occur in e.g., dendrimer capped porphyrins.
